pre-fix-yarn.meaning: "Give us a ring for current hours" narrows the original open-ended contact instruction to a phone call; the dates, prices and tag limits otherwise remain.
pre-fix-yarn.sense: "get first dibs" accurately conveys priority for people unable to cut their own trees.
pre-fix-yarn.authenticity: "Chrissy tree" and "wildlife can find a feed" are idiomatic Australian expressions in context.
pre-fix-yarn.register: "cos it matters", "first dibs" and "does the bush a good turn" make the cumulative voice noticeably heavier than a light level 2.
pre-fix-yarn.tone: "there are no refunds" and "needs another tag" keep the practical purchasing rules clear and serious.
pre-fix-yarn.flow: "So a 15-foot tree, for example, needs two tags" is a smooth, helpful spoken explanation.
pre-fix-yarn.variety: "Chrissy tree" recurs throughout nearly every section, a noticeable repeated device despite other varied idiom.
pre-fix-yarn.essence: "The permit system helps thin out thick stands of skinny little trees" retains the distinctive forest-health explanation beyond the shopping instructions.

current.meaning: "from November 22 through December 20, 2024" preserves even the source's apparently inconsistent year, while "$10 and are non-refundable" retains the purchase conditions.
current.sense: "needs an extra tag" correctly expresses the additional permit requirement.
current.authenticity: "Chrissy tree permits go on sale" is a natural Australian opening without forced idiom.
current.register: "thin out densely populated stands of small-diameter trees" reflects mostly plain administrative prose after the opening, somewhat lighter than level 2.
current.tone: "Make sure you carefully read the overview and need-to-know information" keeps the source's helpful official guidance.
current.flow: "Buying online through recreation.gov adds a $2.50 service fee" reads directly and cleanly.
current.variety: "go on sale", "needs an extra tag" and "priority going to" vary the plain conversational phrasing without repetitive tags.
current.essence: "Removing these trees in designated areas helps other trees grow larger" keeps the conservation rationale and the original information structure.

dinkum-3.meaning: "there's an extra $2.50 service fee on top" and "a 15-foot (4.6 m) tree, say, needs two" retain the costs and tag example with useful unit equivalents.
dinkum-3.sense: "patches of feed for the wildlife" appropriately renders areas providing forage.
dinkum-3.authenticity: "have a proper read" and "get first dibs" sound like natural Australian advice.
dinkum-3.register: "just pop in", "heads up" and "does the bush a good turn" make this a little more conversational than the light level-2 brief, though still controlled and clean.
dinkum-3.tone: "Make sure you have a proper read of the overview and need-to-know info" preserves the original's careful, helpful instruction.
dinkum-3.flow: "Anything taller than 10 feet and/or wider than 5 inches needs an extra tag" handles the technical limits in a readable spoken sentence.
dinkum-3.variety: "Chrissie tree" repeatedly supplies the Australian marker across headings and paragraphs, although the other expressions vary.
dinkum-3.essence: "Local forest health experts pick the areas that'll benefit from thinning" preserves the management rationale and role of expert selection.

summaries.pre-fix-yarn: A clear, complete practical retelling with natural local speech, but a heavier vernacular presence than requested and a small contact-method restriction.
summaries.current: The most restrained and exact version, smoothly preserving every instruction but only faintly Australian after its first line.
summaries.dinkum-3: A faithful, clear local retelling that keeps the practical instructions and conservation rationale; slightly more chatty than the brief.
